issues: Abstract drift risk is elevated: intake does not sufficiently lock object-first behavior.
fixes: Add anti-drift rules and explicit bans on texture-only, atmosphere-first, and abstract-first outcomes.

revised_intake.creative_intent: To conduct a material study focused on achieving a clean matte B4C technical ceramic read, applied to a manufactured object. The primary goal is to preserve the original shape, silhouette, and exact form of the object with minimal transformation, while strictly maintaining a material-only scope.

must_have: readable contour evidence of a manufactured object
exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture
visible edge, rim, bevel, seam, or contour evidence
material visibly attached to the object

composition.framing: Tight framing on the object, preserving full silhouette and form.
composition.camera: Eye-level, direct, focused on the object to highlight material and form.
composition.background: Clean, neutral, non-distracting background to emphasize the subject and its material.

lighting.style: Even, diffuse, to emphasize material texture and form without harsh shadows or highlights.
constraints: No harsh reflections that obscure the matte finish
No obscuring shadows that compromise silhouette or material read
Lighting must enhance the dry, dense quality of the ceramic
color must remain subordinate to material identity
color must follow form then material, never override them
no flat color, always material texture variation
pure white and pure black are forbidden
ceramic off-white must stay warm and broken, never sterile pure white
charcoal black must keep temperature variation, never dead pure black
restrained crimson only in seams, cores, or controlled heat accents
muted earth support only, low saturation material support tones

core_risks: Drift towards abstract compositions or textures, losing the manufactured object read.
Material ambiguity, resulting in reads of forbidden materials.
Loss of original shape or silhouette due to transformation.
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: Maintain a clear, singular manufactured object as the subject.
Prevent any drift towards abstract forms or textures.
Ensure the object's material is unequivocally B4C technical ceramic.
Strictly avoid any visual cues of natural stone, minerals, or soft, pliable materials.
Preserve the exact form and silhouette of the original shape.
No glossy or reflective surfaces that contradict the matte finish.
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
form -> material -> color priority is mandatory
do not allow neon, pure white, pure black, or plastic-clean RGB drift
crimson may appear only as restrained seam/core accent when applicable
do not allow abstract, texture-only, or atmosphere-first subject drift
keep material identity explicit and stable
success_criteria: Immediate and unambiguous readability of a clean matte B4C technical ceramic surface.
The material must clearly belong to a single, identifiable manufactured object.
The object's original shape and silhouette must be perfectly preserved.
No visual ambiguity regarding the material's identity or the object's engineered nature.
The object must appear dry, dense, and technically manufactured.
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
color feels subtractive and pigment-like, never RGB-clean
shadow mass dominates and color remains materially grounded
image does not read as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
revised_intake.direction_summary: Focus on a material study of clean matte B4C technical ceramic, applied to a clearly defined, singular manufactured object. The object's original shape and silhouette must be strictly preserved, ensuring a dry, dense, and engineered readability without any abstract or forbidden material interpretations.
